issue.title: Round printed temperatures to one decimal place (thermo and thermo-table)
issue.problem: Both command-line tools print the raw floating-point result of conv.js, so floating-point noise shows up in the output. At the current head: `node bin/thermo.js 37` prints `98.60000000000001°F`; `node bin/thermo.js -f 98.6` prints `36.99999999999999°C`; `node bin/thermo.js -f 100` prints `37.77777777777778°C`; `node bin/thermo.js 36.6` prints `97.88000000000001°F`. `node bin/table.js` (thermo-table) has the same noise in its F column, e.g. rows `31\t87.80000000000001` and `37\t98.60000000000001`. The library functions cToF/fToC in conv.js return unrounded values, and test/conv.test.js only covers those functions. No test covers the CLI output.
issue.reason: Users read these numbers. Values like 98.60000000000001°F look like a bug and are harder to read than 98.6°F, and the -f direction prints long repeating decimals.
issue.outcome: Every temperature printed by `thermo`, `thermo -f` and `thermo-table` is rounded to one decimal place, with no floating-point noise. The library functions and the CLI usage/error behaviour stay the same.
expect: `node bin/thermo.js 37` prints exactly the line `98.6°F` and exits 0.
`node bin/thermo.js 36.6` prints exactly the line `97.9°F`, and `node bin/thermo.js 100` prints a line that is either `212°F` or `212.0°F`.
`node bin/thermo.js -f 100` prints exactly the line `37.8°C`, and `node bin/thermo.js -f 98.6` prints a line that is either `37°C` or `37.0°C`.

`node bin/table.js 30 40` prints the header line `C\tF` followed by 11 rows for C = 30 through 40. In each row the F value is the Fahrenheit equivalent rounded to one decimal place and has at most one digit after the decimal point. The row for 31 has F 87.8 and the row for 37 has F 98.6.
`node bin/table.js -5 -3` prints rows whose F values are 23, 24.8 and 26.6, each with at most one digit after the decimal point.

Error handling is unchanged: `node bin/thermo.js` with no arguments prints `usage: thermo <celsius>` to stderr and exits 2, and `node bin/thermo.js -f x` prints `usage: thermo -f <fahrenheit>` to stderr and exits 2.
The library is unchanged: `require('./conv.js').cToF(37)` still returns 98.60000000000001 and `fToC(100)` still returns 37.77777777777778, so only printed output is rounded.
`npm test` passes and includes at least one new test that runs or checks the printed CLI output for `thermo 37` (expecting `98.6°F`).

non_goals: Changing the return values of cToF/fToC in conv.js (the library stays at full precision).
Adding flags to choose precision, or changing output units, symbols, the table layout or the defaults (30 to 40).
Changing argument parsing or the usage messages and exit codes.
Publishing a release or bumping the package version.
assumptions: "Temperatures we print" covers all three printed outputs: `thermo <c>`, `thermo -f <f>` and the F column of `thermo-table`. The C column of thermo-table is made of integer inputs and is left as is.
Rounding applies only to presentation in the CLI scripts. The library API keeps full precision so that library callers see no behaviour change.

Whole-number results may print either with or without a trailing `.0` (e.g. `212°F` or `212.0°F`). The request only asks for rounding to one decimal place, so both forms are accepted, but there must never be more than one digit after the point.
Rounding is to nearest (e.g. 97.88 → 97.9, 37.777… → 37.8). Exact .x5 ties and the sign of values that round to zero are not specified and are not tested.
